svg.text: VPC endpoints (PrivateLink + gateway): no NAT Gateway needed
AWS API calls stay on the AWS network
ECS services: desired count 2 per service
ECS services: desired count 2 per service
task role + execution role per service
1 Users resolve the domain in Route 53 and connect over HTTPS: Internet Gateway, optional WAF, then the ALB (ACM certificate).
2 The ALB routes by path (/auth, /orders, /notifications) to Fargate tasks in private subnets across two AZs.
3 Orders and Notifications verify every token with Auth by DNS name through AWS Cloud Map (dashed green arrows).
4 Orders and Notifications read and write their DynamoDB tables through the gateway VPC endpoint.
5 Orders publishes an order.created event to SQS (through the SQS interface endpoint) and does not wait for the result.
6 Notifications consumes the queue at its own pace; messages that keep failing go to the dead-letter queue and raise an alarm.
7 Tasks fetch secrets from Secrets Manager at start-up through an interface endpoint.
8 Fargate pulls the images from ECR (scan on push) through interface endpoints.
9 Container logs and metrics go to CloudWatch, where the alarms are defined.
10 GitHub Actions builds the images, pushes them to ECR and updates the ECS services (OIDC, no stored keys).
Containerized Microservices on Amazon ECS Fargate - Solution Architecture
